clue.text: Broadcast chat on Beeb about British Library jargon

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round, or about, the abbreviation that follows
to broadcast is to scatter widely, so the letters of these words are scattered into a new order

parts.note: BL is the standard abbreviation for the British Library

explanation.surface: A BBC radio programme chats about the British Library in impenetrable jargon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' rearranges CHAT ON BEEB into TECHNOBABE, and 'about' puts that round BL, which sits just before its final E. The Beeb is the BBC.
explanation.definitionFit: Impenetrable technical talk meant to impress or baffle is a kind of jargon, a synonym in informal use.

clue.text: Nuisance follows group unleashing a storm

indicators.note: the nuisance word comes after the trimmed group word
unleashing means letting go, so the letter given by the word a is let out of the group word

parts.note: a team is a group
a pest is a nuisance

explanation.surface: An annoying person trails along behind a gang that whips up a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unleashing' lets the A go from the group word; 'follows' puts the nuisance after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent gale with heavy weather is a storm; the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Girl left one in middle of Atlantic, say

indicators.note: the letters for left and one are placed inside the trimmed ocean word
only the middle of the word is kept, its outer letters dropped

parts.note: the Atlantic is an example of an ocean
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A girl abandoned someone in mid-ocean, out in the Atlantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' trims OCEAN to CEA, and 'in' puts LI inside it. 'say' marks the Atlantic as just one example of an ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Celia is a female first name, so it stands for a girl in crosswords.

clue.text: French article turned up lewd heartless content of strip-club?

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the French article is read from bottom to top

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article, a

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter of the lewd word is removed

parts.note: dirty means lewd

explanation.surface: A French newspaper piece exposes the seedy goings-on at a strip-club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' gives NU from UN; 'heartless' takes the R from DIRTY, leaving DITY. 'article' looks like a newspaper piece but is the grammatical word.
explanation.definitionFit: Bareness is what a striptease ends in, so nakedness is the playful content of a strip-club, flagged by the question mark.

clue.text: Group securing right promotional concept

indicators.note: securing means holding something inside, so the group word holds the letter for right

parts.note: a band is a group

explanation.surface: A pop group locks in the rights to a marketing idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand is the identity or image a company promotes, a marketing idea built around a product.

clue.text: Want hearts engraved in trunk (an attractive feature)?

indicators.note: engraved in means cut into, so these letters are set inside the word for trunk

parts.note: a bole is the trunk of a tree
lack means want, as in need
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games

explanation.surface: Lovers carve hearts into a tree trunk, a charming feature of the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engraved in' sets the want and hearts letters inside the trunk word. The definition plays on attraction: gravity, not charm.
explanation.definitionFit: This region of space has gravity so strong it pulls in even light, so it is literally a highly attractive feature.

clue.text: Realist moved to contain one disease

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the letter for one inside them
moved means the letters of the word are shifted into a new arrangement

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A realist is roused to fight the spread of a disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' turns REALIST into LISTERA, and 'to contain' slips I in before the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: This bacterium causes food poisoning, and its name is loosely used for the illness itself.

clue.text: AB, upset about dodgy tackle, leaves

indicators.note: the reversed letters go around the rearranged fodder
in a down clue upset means the two letters are turned upside down, read in reverse
dodgy means unsound, so the letters are not in their proper order

explanation.surface: A sailor, upset about faulty fishing gear, walks off.
explanation.walkthrough: AB is an able seaman; 'upset' turns it to BA and 'about' wraps it round the scramble signalled by 'dodgy'. 'leaves' looks like a verb but means tea leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaves are what tea is brewed from, and this is the fully oxidised everyday kind.

clue.text: Surprised comment over a barrel-maker

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: coo is an exclamation of surprise
per means a, as in so much a head

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise at a cask maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' here means 'per', as in 'ten pounds a day'. COO is a British exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooper is a craftsman who builds and repairs casks and barrels.

clue.text: Mother keeping payment back to drive sob story?

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the mother word keeps the following pieces within it

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: back means the payment word is read in reverse

parts.note: the dole is a state payment to the unemployed
to ram is to drive forcefully

explanation.surface: A mother holds back a payment to drive home a tearful tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the payment word round, and 'keeping' has the mother word hold that and the drive word inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama that exaggerates emotion to tug at feelings is a tearjerker, which the question mark lets stand as a sob story.

clue.text: Gunfire volume filling most of room

indicators.note: filling means occupying the inside, so the letter for volume goes within the shortened room word
most of means the last letter of the room word is dropped

parts.note: a salon is a reception room

explanation.surface: The roar of gunfire fills almost the whole room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims SALON to SALO, and V goes between L and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A simultaneous discharge of several guns is a salvo, a burst of gunfire.

clue.text: Not initially annoyed about computer key placed in high position

indicators.note: the trimmed word goes around the computer key
not initially means the first letter of the annoyed word is dropped

parts.note: vexed means annoyed
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: Someone is irritated about a computer key being put up out of reach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not initially' gives EXED; 'about' wraps it round the key.
explanation.definitionFit: Exalted means raised to a lofty rank or status, an elevated standing.

clue.text: Was aware endless speed knocked back bone in leg

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: knew means was aware

indicators.note: knocked back means the speed word is read in reverse

parts.note: pace means speed

explanation.surface: Someone knew that a fast pace had wrecked a bone in their leg.
explanation.walkthrough: KNEW without its last letter is KNE; PACE reversed is ECAP.
explanation.definitionFit: The patella, the small bone at the front of the knee joint, sits in the leg.

clue.text: Bodies of water spurned by new seamen

indicators.note: spurned by means rejected by, so the letter for new is thrown out of the water word

parts.note: tarns are small mountain lakes

explanation.surface: Novice sailors turn their backs on lakes.
explanation.walkthrough: TARNS, small mountain lakes found in northern England, lose N.
explanation.definitionFit: Tar is old slang for a sailor, from the tarred clothing sailors wore.

clue.text: Lord many perceived thus?

indicators.note: the words are seen in the jumbled manner the solution describes, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about how a lord might be seen by the masses.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is self-referential: the letters of LORD MANY, seen haphazardly, make the solution, which is also how they are seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Haphazardly or without order is how scrambled letters appear, so the adverb describes the jumbled view of the words.

clue.text: I go on working with treaty, mostly?

definitions.text: I go on working with treaty, mostly?

indicators.note: working means being worked over, so the letters are reshaped into a new order
mostly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: the word is taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A diplomat says they keep working away at a treaty, mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims TREATY to TREAT; 'working' rearranges IGOON with TREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomat who spends their time hammering out a treaty is a deal-maker, exactly what the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Close river incorporating an opening for competitor's stamina

parts.note: end means close, as in the conclusion

indicators.note: incorporating means taking in, so the river word takes the following letters inside it

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

indicators.note: the opening of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A competitor's stamina is tested near the end of a river course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening for' takes the first letter of competitor's; 'incorporating' sets it with 'an' inside the Yorkshire river.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is the capacity to keep going under strain, which is lasting power or endurance.

clue.text: Feel bad about objection over working plant

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first part sits above the second
the ailing word goes around the objection word

parts.note: to ail is to feel unwell
a but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts
on means working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: Someone feels guilty about raising an objection to working on a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the feeling-bad word round the objection; 'over' stacks it above the working word in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Abutilon is a genus of flowering shrubs in the mallow family, often called Indian mallow.

clue.text: Economic plan I ditch after reflection being swamped by abuse, see?

indicators.note: being swamped by means sunk in, so the reversed letters go inside the abuse word

parts.note: mud is abuse, as in slinging mud

indicators.note: reflection reverses, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: to bin is to ditch, throw away
to get is to see, understand

explanation.surface: After thinking it over, a minister scraps an economic plan buried in abuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after reflection' gives NIBI, which 'being swamped by' sinks into the abuse word. A mini-budget is a British term for a small emergency budget between main ones.
explanation.definitionFit: A mini-budget is a small government fiscal statement, an economic plan announced between the annual budgets.

clue.text: Unknown stink about price rises for potato

indicators.note: in a down clue rises means the letters are read upwards, in reverse
the stink word goes around the price abbreviation

parts.note: hum is slang for a bad smell
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A mysterious row over rising prices for potatoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives HPRUM and 'rises' turns it to MURPH; the unknown, first in the clue, goes last, since only the bracketed part rises.
explanation.definitionFit: Murphy is an informal, originally Irish, slang name for a potato.

clue.text: Hard to avoid manhunt in legal matter

indicators.note: to avoid means to keep out, so the letter for hard is removed from the manhunt word

parts.note: a chase is a pursuit, a manhunt
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Avoiding a manhunt is hard work in a court matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A case is a lawsuit, a matter brought before a court of law.

clue.text: Consumer continues picking up last three

indicators.note: in a down clue picking up means raising, so only the final three letters are read upwards

parts.note: endures means continues

explanation.surface: A shopper keeps on picking up the last three items.
explanation.walkthrough: ENDURES has its last three letters, RES, reversed to SER.
explanation.definitionFit: The final buyer who uses a product, rather than reselling it, is its consumer.

clue.text: Turned chill, suppressing one supplier of information

parts.note: milk that has turned has gone sour

indicators.note: suppressing means holding down and out, so the letter for one is removed

parts.note: ice means chill
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone turned frosty, holding back one informant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suppressing' removes the one from the chill word. 'Turned' reads as a verb of change but means gone off, like milk.
explanation.definitionFit: A source is a person or document that supplies facts, as a journalist's informant.

clue.text: List includes duck's-egg? Not from me

indicators.note: includes means holds within, so the list word takes the round letter inside it

parts.note: a roster is a list of duties
a duck's egg is a zero score, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A shopping list includes a duck egg, but don't expect one from me.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck's egg is a cricket duck, a score of nought, so O. The definition is a cockerel speaking: a male bird lays no eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockerel cannot lay eggs, so an egg is never from this male bird, which is the playful definition.

clue.text: Cat burglar finally apprehended in flat after a sign

indicators.note: after means the flat piece follows the sign piece

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac

indicators.note: apprehended in means caught inside, so the burglar's last letter is held within the flat word

parts.note: a pad is a flat, a home

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the burglar word

explanation.surface: A cat burglar is finally caught in a flat, after a sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' picks R and 'apprehended in' holds it in the flat word; 'after' puts that behind the zodiac sign. 'Cat burglar' reads as one phrase, but 'Cat' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The leopard is a large spotted cat of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Takes up line, getting chasms after river falls

indicators.note: falls means drops away, so the river letter falls out of the chasms word

parts.note: rifts are chasms or clefts

explanation.surface: A climber takes up a line across chasms below a river's waterfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falls' drops the river letter from the chasms word, leaving IFTS. 'falls' looks like waterfalls but signals the drop.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something is to raise it, so lifts means takes up.

clue.text: Twelve letters left for island

parts.note: the first twelve letters of the alphabet run from A to L

explanation.surface: Twelve letters have been left for an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The twelve letters A, B, C ... L are written as A TO L.
explanation.definitionFit: An atoll is a ring-shaped coral reef or island enclosing a lagoon.

clue.text: Dining area accommodates a way of preparing meat

indicators.note: accommodates means makes room for, so the dining area takes the a inside it

parts.note: a hall is a dining room, as in a college hall

explanation.surface: A dining room makes space for a particular way of preparing meat.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes between the two Ls of HALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Halal meat is slaughtered and prepared according to Islamic law, so the term names a method of preparation.

clue.text: Sofa besmirched with urine? Nasty

indicators.note: besmirched means soiled and spoiled, so the letters of these words are messed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A sofa stained with urine is a nasty sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefarious means wicked or villainous, so it overlaps with nasty in the sense of evil.

clue.text: Rattles liner at sea covering a great distance

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of these words are put in disorder

explanation.surface: A storm rattles an ocean liner as it covers a vast distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Interstellar means between the stars, spanning vast stretches of space.
